definition_md: A 3-2 count with three balls and two strikes.
when_to_use_md: Use when the count is explicitly 3-2 or when a plate appearance reaches a 3-2 state.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use for any other count state.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'full count'. In org surfaces, '3-2 count' is also acceptable.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not substitute vague language like 'critical count' unless leverage is separately supported.
examples: The challenge kept the plate appearance at a full count.

definition_md: A baserunner on second and/or third base.
when_to_use_md: Use when the situation specifically involves second and/or third being occupied.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if only first base is occupied.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'runners in scoring position'. In org mode, 'RISP' is acceptable sparingly.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not force the acronym in fan-facing copy.
examples: They stranded runners in scoring position in the middle innings.

definition_md: First, second, and third base are all occupied.
when_to_use_md: Use when all three bases are occupied.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use when fewer than three bases are occupied.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use generic traffic language when the exact state is bases loaded.
examples: The overturn came with the bases loaded in a one-run game.

definition_md: A game in which a team allows no runs; pitcher-level usage must respect scoring context.
when_to_use_md: Use when the evidence supports a scoreless game outcome.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not call an individual pitcher outing a shutout unless the evidence supports pitcher-level credit framing.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'shutout', 'held them scoreless', or 'blanked' when appropriate.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use loosely for partial scoreless stretches.
examples: They finished the game with a team shutout.

definition_md: A game-ending play in which the home team takes the lead in the bottom of the final inning or extras.
when_to_use_md: Use only when the home team wins on the final play.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use for any other late-inning scoring play.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use for non-final late rallies.
examples: The game ended on a walk-off after the review sequence.

definition_md: Innings played beyond the ninth inning in a tied game.
when_to_use_md: Use when the game extends beyond regulation.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use before the game reaches the 10th inning.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'extra innings'. 'Free baseball' may be allowed in fan mode sparingly.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use casual phrasing in org mode.
examples: The challenge profile changed once the game moved into extra innings.

definition_md: The game-state importance of a moment, often tied to win expectancy swing potential.
when_to_use_md: Use when the game-state context or model output explicitly supports importance framing.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use as empty drama language without supporting context.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'leverage', 'high-leverage spot', or specific leverage bands when available.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use 'huge moment' if leverage framing is available and more precise.
examples: This was a high-leverage review window in the late innings.

definition_md: A strikeout in which the batter does not swing and strike three is called by the umpire.
when_to_use_md: Use when the terminal outcome is a strikeout looking.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use for swinging strikeouts.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use for generic strikeouts unless the called/swinging distinction is supported.
examples: The overturned call removed a called third strike from the plate appearance.

definition_md: A strikeout in which the batter swings through strike three.
when_to_use_md: Use when the terminal outcome is a swinging strikeout.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use for called strikeouts.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'swinging strikeout' or 'whiffed for strike three' in fan mode sparingly.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use colloquial language in org mode unless style pack allows it.
examples: The count moved away from a called-strikeout path and ended later in a swinging strikeout.

definition_md: A play that records two outs.
when_to_use_md: Use when two outs are recorded on the same play.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use for sequential outs across separate plays.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not reduce it to vague 'they got out of it' language if double-play evidence exists.
examples: The inning-ending double play erased the remaining threat.

definition_md: Runners who remain on base when the half-inning ends.
when_to_use_md: Use when discussing stranded runners or missed opportunities.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not force the phrase when no runners were stranded.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use generic 'missed it' language if stranded-runner framing is the real baseball takeaway.
examples: They left the tying run on base after the overturned call.

definition_md: Baserunners left on base for a relief pitcher by the previous pitcher.
when_to_use_md: Use when relief context is specifically relevant.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use when no pitching change context exists.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use if bullpen context is not actually in evidence.
examples: The reliever entered with inherited runners and a live review situation.

definition_md: A game state in which a reliever can earn a save under official scoring rules.
when_to_use_md: Use when bullpen context explicitly supports it.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use loosely for any late-game lead.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not imply official save logic when not supported.
examples: The late review happened in a save situation.

definition_md: A reliever loses a lead in a save opportunity.
when_to_use_md: Use only when official save-opportunity context exists and the lead is lost.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use for generic late-game scoring allowed.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use without save-opportunity context.
examples: The overturned call extended the inning before the eventual blown save.

definition_md: An ongoing attempt to complete a no-hitter.
when_to_use_md: Use when a pitcher or staff has not allowed a hit and the game is still in progress.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use after a hit is allowed or if the evidence is only retrospective without that context.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use dramatic no-hit framing after the bid has ended.
examples: The review sequence came during a no-hit bid.

definition_md: A starting pitcher throws at least six innings and allows three earned runs or fewer.
when_to_use_md: Use only if the evidence supports the official threshold.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use loosely for any strong outing.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not imply the official stat if the threshold is not met.
examples: Despite the review traffic, he still finished with a quality start.

definition_md: A game in which a team uses multiple relievers rather than a traditional starter workload.
when_to_use_md: Use when the evidence clearly supports that framing.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use just because a starter exited early once.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not overuse when pitcher usage does not fit the pattern.
examples: The challenge profile mattered more because it was effectively a bullpen game.

definition_md: A style emphasizing singles, bunts, steals, and run manufacturing over pure slugging.
when_to_use_md: Use when the evidence actually supports run-manufacturing style framing.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not force it when the game was driven by slugging or non-contextual offense.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'small ball' only when stylistically warranted.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use as filler baseball color.
examples: The offense leaned more small ball than power in the late innings.

definition_md: A high-scoring game with heavy offensive output.
when_to_use_md: Use in fan-facing contexts when evidence clearly supports a high-scoring game narrative.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use for middling or low-scoring games.
banned_phrasing_md: Avoid in org mode unless style pack explicitly allows it.
examples: The review sequences were part of a broader slugfest.

definition_md: An inning or half-inning in which no runs score.
when_to_use_md: Use for inning-level scoreless outcomes.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if runs scored.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use if more specific outcome language is available and better suited.
examples: The overturned call helped preserve a scoreless frame.

definition_md: An inning with no baserunners or no real traffic depending on context.
when_to_use_md: Use cautiously when the inning was tidy and the style pack allows looser phrasing.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if the inning included meaningful traffic.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'clean inning' only when clearly supported.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use if runners reached or the evidence shows sustained pressure.
examples: He followed the review sequence with a clean inning.

definition_md: Repeated baserunner pressure in an inning or stretch.
when_to_use_md: Use when the evidence supports multiple baserunners or sustained baserunner pressure.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use for isolated baserunner events.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'traffic on the bases' or 'traffic' sparingly.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use as generic pressure language without baserunner context.
examples: The overturned call added traffic on the bases in a leverage spot.

definition_md: A hitter or sequence that creates offensive opportunities for the middle of the order.
when_to_use_md: Use when lineup-context language is genuinely relevant.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not force lineup-role narrative if not supported by context.
banned_phrasing_md: Avoid in dense org contexts unless it clarifies lineup role.
examples: The leadoff spot functioned as the table setter in the early innings.

definition_md: An additional run that extends a lead and provides margin.
when_to_use_md: Use when a lead-extending run adds meaningful margin.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use for every late score if margin context is not meaningful.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use if the run did not materially change margin or context.
examples: The overturned count helped set up an insurance run in the eighth.

definition_md: The run that gives the winning team a lead it never relinquishes.
when_to_use_md: Use when that specific scoring logic is supported.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use loosely for any go-ahead run if the lead changes again later.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use without final-game outcome support.
examples: The review sequence helped preserve the game-winning run.

definition_md: Overturned Call in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when a reviewed call is reversed.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if no review occurred or the review is still in progress.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'the call was overturned' or 'the challenge reversed the call'.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not default to blame language like 'the ump blew it'.
examples: Example AiBS usage for overturned call.

definition_md: Confirmed Call in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when a reviewed call stands after review.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use for non-reviewed calls.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'the call was confirmed' or 'the call stood after review'.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not imply a correction if the call was confirmed.
examples: Example AiBS usage for confirmed call.

definition_md: Challenged Call in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when describing the specific call that triggered ABS review.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if there was no challenge.
banned_phrasing_md: Avoid vague wording when the challenged-call framing is available.
examples: Example AiBS usage for challenged call.

definition_md: Reviewed Call in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use as neutral review framing when a pitch/call entered the review process.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use to imply a result before the result is known.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not overstate review outcome from neutral review language.
examples: Example AiBS usage for reviewed call.

definition_md: Successful Challenge in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when the challenging team gets an overturn.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if the challenge fails or the result is unknown.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use generic winning language when precise challenge-success framing exists.
examples: Example AiBS usage for successful challenge.

definition_md: Failed Challenge in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when the challenging team does not get an overturn.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if the challenge is successful or unresolved.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not over-dramatize with 'disaster' language.
examples: Example AiBS usage for failed challenge.

definition_md: Challenge Burn in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when an unsuccessful challenge clearly consumes inventory and strategic framing is appropriate.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use in neutral recaps unless inventory consequence is central.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'burned a challenge' or 'spent a challenge without changing the count'.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not say 'wasted challenge' unless poor-process evidence exists.
examples: Example AiBS usage for challenge burn.

definition_md: Call Reversal in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when review changes the original ruling.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if the reviewed call stands.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not imply reversal if the call was confirmed.
examples: Example AiBS usage for call reversal.

definition_md: Call Stands in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when the original ruling remains in place after review.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use when the call is overturned.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not imply a reversal.
examples: Example AiBS usage for call stands.

definition_md: Count Flip in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when review materially changes the count state.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if the review outcome does not change the count in a meaningful way.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'flipped the count' or 'changed the plate appearance state'.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use if the count effect is neutral or absent.
examples: Example AiBS usage for count flip.

definition_md: Count Swing in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when the count changes in a meaningful directional way after review.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if there is no directional count movement.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not overstate if the shift is minimal or neutral.
examples: Example AiBS usage for count swing.

definition_md: Corrected Count in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when discussing the count after the reviewed correction.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if the corrected state is not available.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not invent a corrected count.
examples: Example AiBS usage for corrected count.

definition_md: Held Count in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when the original count remains after review or non-overturn.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if the review actually changes the count.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use if the count changed.
examples: Example AiBS usage for held count.

definition_md: Terminal Count in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when the count result immediately creates a walk or strikeout outcome.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use on non-terminal states.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer 'terminal count' only in org/dense analytical surfaces.
banned_phrasing_md: Avoid jargon-heavy usage in fan mode unless supported by style pack.
examples: Example AiBS usage for terminal count.

definition_md: Full-Count Pressure in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when a reviewed decision occurs in a 3-2 count with heightened leverage.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if the count is not full or the pressure framing is unsupported.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use generic pressure language if full-count framing is available and more precise.
examples: Example AiBS usage for full-count pressure.

definition_md: Challenge Value in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when the product is discussing modeled review value or consequence.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if no value model or consequence framing exists.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not substitute vague 'good challenge' language when explicit value framing is available.
examples: Example AiBS usage for challenge value.

definition_md: Expected Challenge Value in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when modeled expected benefit is present.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use when only realized outcome is available.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not blur expected and realized value.
examples: Example AiBS usage for expected challenge value.

definition_md: Realized Challenge Value in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when the actual realized game-state outcome of the challenge is known.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if only modeled expected value exists.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not collapse realized and expected values into one term.
examples: Example AiBS usage for realized challenge value.

definition_md: Decision Surplus in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when process outperforms outcome or vice versa within an expected-vs-realized framework.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use without explicit process-vs-result modeling.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not call something 'smart process' without model support.
examples: Example AiBS usage for decision surplus.

definition_md: Decision Cost in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when a review decision carries modeled downside or opportunity cost.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use without explicit decision-cost framing.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not imply cost without evidence.
examples: Example AiBS usage for decision cost.

definition_md: Review Worthiness in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when evaluating whether a spot warranted review consideration.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if no process-oriented framing exists.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not overstate as obvious without evidence.
examples: Example AiBS usage for review worthiness.

definition_md: Inventory Discipline in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when a team shows selective or efficient challenge usage.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if there is no inventory pattern evidence.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use generic 'smart team' language instead.
examples: Example AiBS usage for inventory discipline.

definition_md: Inventory Deployment in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when describing when and where teams spend review inventory.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if challenge spending pattern is not part of the question/evidence.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not flatten to 'used challenges' when deployment framing matters.
examples: Example AiBS usage for inventory deployment.

definition_md: Challenge Opportunity in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when describing situations that present a potentially valuable review window.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if no genuine review window existed.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not treat every reviewed pitch as an opportunity if the context did not warrant it.
examples: Example AiBS usage for challenge opportunity.

definition_md: Challenge Traffic in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when describing clustering or volume of reviews in certain contexts or lanes.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use for isolated reviewed pitches.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use generic 'a lot of reviews' when traffic framing is more specific.
examples: Example AiBS usage for challenge traffic.

definition_md: Review Exposure in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when discussing how often an umpire or context enters review danger zones.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if there is no review clustering or exposure evidence.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not overstate with blame language.
examples: Example AiBS usage for review exposure.

definition_md: Zone Vulnerability in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when certain lanes or edges show elevated overturn or review pressure.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if location data does not support it.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not say an umpire is 'bad in that zone' unless the evidence specifically supports that stronger claim.
examples: Example AiBS usage for zone vulnerability.

definition_md: Overturn Lane in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when a specific zone lane shows elevated overturn behavior.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use without lane-specific evidence.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not invent lanes or hotspots.
examples: Example AiBS usage for overturn lane.

definition_md: Challenge Rhythm in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when challenge exposure changes inning by inning or over game flow.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if no temporal pattern exists.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not force rhythm language onto noisy or tiny samples.
examples: Example AiBS usage for challenge rhythm.

definition_md: Challenge Management in AiBS challenge-era analysis.
when_to_use_md: Use when evaluating team challenge process across a game or sample.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not use if inventory strategy is not part of the evidence.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not reduce all challenge decisions to outcome-only framing.
examples: Example AiBS usage for challenge management.

definition_md: Anti-pattern control for generic incorrectness language.
when_to_use_md: Avoid generic 'the umpire got it wrong' phrasing when a more precise review outcome exists.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not inject this card unless the semantic context makes the anti-pattern risk relevant.
preferred_phrasing_md: If review outcome is known, prefer overturned/confirmed/challenged-call language.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not use blame-heavy language unless a stronger evaluative frame is explicitly supported.
examples: Block or steer away from generic incorrectness language in the relevant contexts.

definition_md: Anti-pattern control for deterministic strategy language.
when_to_use_md: Avoid acting as if challenge strategy was obviously correct or incorrect without process evidence.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not inject this card unless the semantic context makes the anti-pattern risk relevant.
preferred_phrasing_md: Use modeled-value or process language when available.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not say 'they absolutely had to challenge' without support.
examples: Block or steer away from deterministic strategy language in the relevant contexts.

definition_md: Anti-pattern control for fake certainty on value.
when_to_use_md: Avoid over-certainty on expected or realized challenge value.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not inject this card unless the semantic context makes the anti-pattern risk relevant.
preferred_phrasing_md: Use directional or modeled language when confidence is limited.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not say 'this was absolutely worth it' if the value signal is mixed or thin.
examples: Block or steer away from fake certainty on value in the relevant contexts.

definition_md: Anti-pattern control for review result overclaim.
when_to_use_md: Avoid letting the review result stand in for full strategic judgment.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not inject this card unless the semantic context makes the anti-pattern risk relevant.
preferred_phrasing_md: Separate review result from process quality.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not say a successful challenge proves strong process on its own.
examples: Block or steer away from review result overclaim in the relevant contexts.

definition_md: Anti-pattern control for umpire blame language.
when_to_use_md: Avoid casual blame language about the umpire.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not inject this card unless the semantic context makes the anti-pattern risk relevant.
preferred_phrasing_md: Prefer exposure, traffic, vulnerability, or reviewed-outcome framing.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not say 'the ump was bad all night' without explicit evidence.
examples: Block or steer away from umpire blame language in the relevant contexts.

definition_md: Anti-pattern control for casual overdramatization.
when_to_use_md: Avoid casual overdramatization when precise baseball language is available.
when_not_to_use_md: Do not inject this card unless the semantic context makes the anti-pattern risk relevant.
banned_phrasing_md: Do not force slang or melodrama into analytical surfaces.
examples: Block or steer away from casual overdramatization in the relevant contexts.
